pharm: Selectively and persistently stimulates beta2-adrenergic receptors on airway smooth muscle, increasing intracellular cyclic AMP and producing prolonged (~12 hour) bronchodilation; the long lipophilic side chain anchors it near the receptor for sustained action with a slow onset.
quick: 1 inhalation (50 mcg dry powder) twice daily, ~12 hours apart
Use only if benefit justifies risk; controlled asthma is important in pregnancy
Caution; likely small amounts in milk - weigh benefit
Use with caution in hepatic impairment (reduced clearance)
Asthma control, FEV1/peak flow, heart rate, potassium, rescue-inhaler use
summary: Salmeterol is a long-acting, selective beta2-adrenergic agonist (LABA) inhaled for the maintenance bronchodilator treatment of asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and for the prevention of exercise-induced bronchospasm. It has a slow onset and a long (~12-hour) duration, so it is dosed twice daily and must NOT be used to relieve acute bronchospasm (it is not a rescue medication). It carries a boxed warning that LABA monotherapy increases the risk of asthma-related death; therefore in asthma it must always be used in combination with an inhaled corticosteroid and never as the sole controller. In COPD it may be used as monotherapy or with other agents. Class effects include tachycardia, tremor, hypokalemia, and the risk of paradoxical bronchospasm.
indications: Long-term maintenance treatment of asthma in patients aged >=4 years, ONLY in combination with an inhaled corticosteroid (as a fixed-dose combination preferred)
Prevention of exercise-induced bronchospasm in patients aged >=4 years
Long-term maintenance bronchodilator treatment of airflow obstruction in COPD, including chronic bronchitis and emphysema

dosage.d: 1 inhalation (50 mcg) twice daily, about 12 hours apart
dosage.n: Must be combined with an inhaled corticosteroid; not for acute relief

dosage.d: 1 inhalation (50 mcg) twice daily, about 12 hours apart
1 inhalation (50 mcg) at least 30 minutes before exercise

Only as fixed-combination with ICS; not as monotherapy

admin: Inhale the dry powder deeply and rapidly through the device; do not exhale into the device
Use on a regular twice-daily schedule about 12 hours apart - do NOT use to relieve sudden breathing difficulty
For asthma, always use together with an inhaled corticosteroid (prefer a fixed-dose combination)
For exercise prevention, take at least 30 minutes before activity and not within 12 hours of a maintenance dose
Always have a short-acting beta-agonist (e.g., albuterol) available for acute symptoms; do not exceed the prescribed dose
moa: Salmeterol is a selective long-acting beta2-adrenergic receptor agonist. Stimulation of beta2-receptors on bronchial smooth muscle activates adenylate cyclase, raising intracellular cyclic AMP, which relaxes airway smooth muscle and inhibits release of mediators of immediate hypersensitivity from cells, especially mast cells. Its long lipophilic side chain binds within an 'exosite' region near the active receptor site, allowing persistent receptor stimulation and producing a prolonged bronchodilator effect (~12 hours) with a comparatively slow onset, which is why it is unsuitable for acute relief.

absolute: Primary treatment of status asthmaticus or acute episodes of asthma/COPD requiring intensive measures
Monotherapy in asthma (must be used with an inhaled corticosteroid)
Known severe hypersensitivity to salmeterol, milk proteins (powder formulations), or excipients
relative: Cardiovascular disorders, especially coronary insufficiency, arrhythmias, and hypertension
Patients unusually responsive to sympathomimetic amines or with hypokalemia
monitor: Asthma/COPD control and rescue inhaler use
Heart rate, blood pressure, and ECG in cardiac patients
Signs of paradoxical bronchospasm or deterioration

preg: There are no adequate well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Salmeterol should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk. Maintaining good asthma control is important, as uncontrolled asthma poses risks to mother and fetus.
lact: It is not known whether salmeterol is excreted in human milk; plasma levels after inhalation are low, and small amounts are likely present in milk. Use with caution in nursing mothers, weighing the benefit of breastfeeding against the benefit of therapy.
renal: No specific dosage adjustment is required for renal impairment.
hepatic: Salmeterol is extensively metabolized by hydroxylation (CYP3A4); use with caution in patients with hepatic impairment, in whom clearance may be reduced.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, ritonavir, clarithromycin) - markedly increase salmeterol exposure with risk of QT prolongation and cardiovascular effects; avoid concomitant use
Non-selective beta-blockers - block the bronchodilator effect and may provoke severe bronchospasm; avoid unless no alternative
moderate: Other adrenergic drugs - additive cardiovascular and sympathomimetic effects
Diuretics (non-potassium-sparing) - additive hypokalemia and ECG changes
Drugs that prolong the QT interval / MAO inhibitors / tricyclic antidepressants - potentiate cardiovascular effects of beta-agonists
minor: Xanthine derivatives and corticosteroids - additive hypokalemia
interactions.diagnostics: May cause transient decreases in serum potassium and increases in glucose; can affect ECG (QTc).

serious: Asthma-related death (LABA monotherapy in asthma - boxed warning)
rare: Immediate hypersensitivity reactions (rash, urticaria, angioedema, anaphylaxis)

monitoring: Asthma/COPD symptom control and frequency of rescue-inhaler use
Heart rate and blood pressure, particularly in cardiac patients
Serum potassium and blood glucose where indicated
Signs of deteriorating disease prompting reassessment of therapy
counsel: Use this inhaler regularly twice a day, about 12 hours apart - it is NOT a rescue inhaler and will not relieve a sudden attack
Always keep your fast-acting reliever inhaler (such as albuterol) with you for sudden symptoms
If you have asthma, you must also use a steroid inhaler as prescribed - never use salmeterol alone for asthma
Tell your doctor if your breathing gets worse, you need your reliever more often, or this inhaler seems less effective
Report fast or irregular heartbeat, marked tremor, or muscle cramps
For preventing exercise-related symptoms, use at least 30 minutes before exercise and not within 12 hours of a regular dose
pk: Bronchodilation within ~10-20 minutes; slow onset (not for acute relief)
Store at controlled room temperature; keep dry powder device dry and capped
pearls: BOXED WARNING: LABA monotherapy increases asthma-related death - in asthma always combine with an inhaled corticosteroid, never use alone
Slow onset, long duration - strictly a maintenance bronchodilator, NOT a rescue inhaler; ensure patient has a SABA
Avoid strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ritonavir, ketoconazole) - large rises in exposure with QT/cardiac risk
Class effects: tremor, tachycardia, hypokalemia, hyperglycemia - watch in cardiac/diabetic patients
Watch for paradoxical bronchospasm immediately after inhalation - discontinue if it occurs
In COPD, may be used as monotherapy; asthma rule (ICS pairing) does not apply to COPD
missed: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip the missed dose. Do not take two doses at once or use the inhaler more than twice a day.
overdose: Overdose can cause exaggerated beta-adrenergic effects: marked tachycardia, arrhythmias, tremor, hypertension or hypotension, hypokalemia, hyperglycemia, headache, and possibly cardiac arrest or death. Discontinue salmeterol, provide supportive therapy, and consider judicious use of a cardioselective beta-blocker (with caution in patients with bronchospasm). Monitor cardiac status and potassium.
